editor that opened at line 1. Capture the top visible line and the
visible cursor by line number, then restore them in the edit editor and
focus it, so a reviewer can change the line they were reading.

commit.message:
fix(review): keep a review panic inside its run and test the run's bounds

A panic in a review goroutine crashed the process, since the scheduler's
recovery covers only the goroutine that called RunOnce. The concurrent
step is now reviewUnits, which records a panic as that unit's error, and
its cap, its collect-all behavior, and the sheet bound are tested on
their own. A database a spec names twice is reviewed once. The failing
model in the lifecycle test is a local stub instead of a real DNS lookup.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(review): run the AI review and post its findings

AIReviewExecutor loads the workspace and project instructions, reviews
each spec's sheet once per database with that database's facts in the
prompt, and posts every finding as an open thread on the sheet, named as
the AI reviewer's result and listing the databases it applies to. The
same title on the same line across databases is one thread with the
highest priority among them. Up to 8 reviews of one run call the model
at once, a sheet over 256 KiB is reported as not reviewed, and a failed
database fails the run with the collect-all message the rule review uses.

The reviewer runs without tools until the read and search tools land:
the prompt says so and asks the model to list what it could not check in
notes, which the executor logs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(frontend): pin the silent account lists and the workload identity email

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(frontend): let the server gate actor lists and offer typed accounts

- List service accounts and workload identities with a silent context
  instead of copying their list permissions on the client. A denied list
  is dropped instead of redirecting to /403, and the server's check is
  the only gate.
- Offer a typed service account or workload identity email as its
  account even when no list returns it. From the workspace page the lists
  cannot reach another project's accounts, or deleted ones.
- Read the actor value through one helper in both the search and the
  filter, so a lowercased prefix committed with Enter still filters.
- Give the column-resize handle no z-index, and move its tests beside it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(frontend): find every actor kind in the audit log actor filter

The Actor filter searched service accounts and workload identities only
behind a case-sensitive "serviceAccounts/" or "workloadIdentities/"
prefix, but AdvancedSearch lowercases the keyword before it searches,
so every search fell back to users. A typed "users/<email>" also missed,
because the account lists match on email, not on the resource name.

Search users, service accounts and workload identities together on one
keyword, as AccountMultiSelect does, after stripping any resource prefix
regardless of case. Drop the prefix instructions from the hint.

Lower the column-resize handle from z-10 to z-1. It sits inside its own
header cell since #20936, so z-10 only made it paint over inline popups
such as the search menu.

Fixes BYT-10291.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(e2e): prove the task-run log folds a lock-timeout retry

Two plan-detail tests run a statement that times out on a lock another
session holds, once and then twice. They check that the log folds the
failed attempts into one closed "Previous attempts" row above the final
green sections, and that the failed attempt's error entry is still behind
it.

A sequence in the fixture schema counts executions, so exactly N attempts
fail and the next one waits for the lock, whatever the timing. The lock is
released once the umbrella reads "retrying".

- psql: spawnPsql holds a session open by writing its SQL to stdin;
  killing the process ends the session and rolls it back.
- plan-helpers: setPermissiveGates and waitForRollout, now shared with the
  lifecycle spec.
- api-client: updateProjectSettings passes executionRetryPolicy through.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(frontend): fold retried attempts into one row in the task-run log

When the PostgreSQL driver retries a statement after a lock timeout, the
log showed each failed attempt as red sections beside the final one, so a
run that passed read like one that failed. The superseded attempts now
fold into one gray "Previous attempts" row above the final attempt's
sections; only the final attempt's failure is state.

- model: a retry scope is a run of attempt material (transaction control,
  command execute, retry info), and each retry marker closes one attempt.
  Row ids stay positional. The failure mark is picked once per context,
  before the cut, because an attempt on its own has lost the marker that
  supersedes its failure.
- hook: expansion is derived rather than stored. A failed section is open
  by default and the umbrella and attempt rows are closed. The reset runs
  in render when the marker count changes, so no unrelated section opens
  as the list regroups.
- viewer: the row list and the sole section remount on that same key,
  which resets load-more with the regrouping. Statement folds are keyed
  by entry and seeded on the run alone, so they survive the marker.
- LogRows: section rows and the history rows on the shared Collapsible.
  The "retrying" note shows only while the run is running.
- The unused "Retry" section label and retry-attempt detail are removed,
  and the hook's tests move beside the hook.

Design: docs/design/task-run-log-previous-attempts.md (BYT-9993).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs(design): record what implementing previous attempts settled

Implementing the design settled four points it had left open.

- Every failed section opens by default, a superseded one included. The
  umbrella and attempt rows stay closed, so superseded material stays out
  of view until the reader opens its attempt.
- The retrying note reads the run status. A run whose server stopped
  mid-attempt fails with its last command unanswered, and only the status
  tells that apart from an attempt in flight.
- The derivation assumes a complete log. The driver only warns when a log
  write fails, and a lost write reads as it did before this change.
- The marker-count reset also covers each section's load-more state, by
  remounting the row list on the same key.

It also adds SCHEMA_DUMP to the entry inventory and points the
implementation outline at the files that shipped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(e2e): fill the log with SELECTs so the journey leaves no schema behind

Codex round 2 (P2): the nine successes were `ALTER TABLE employee ADD
COLUMN …`, which left a column each on the shared sample table with no
teardown. They exist only to fill the section's box with rows, so make them
`SELECT '<marker>';` — nothing to create, nothing to drop, and each row keeps
a marker of its own for the copy assertion. The file's older tests keep
their DDL: there the schema change is what is under test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(frontend): let the fold control keep the shared xs padding

Codex round 1 (P1): `px-1` on the fold button overrode the shared `xs`
Button's inline padding, making it a one-off 22px control in feature code.
The override was copied from `CopyButton`, which may own its contract as a
shared primitive; feature code may not. Drop it and widen the reserved slot
from 24px to 28px so the control fits at its own width. The suggested
shared icon-only variant is a design-system change with cross-surface reach;
removing the override resolves the finding without it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(frontend): unfold and copy a statement in the task-run log

Implements docs/design/task-run-log-statement-unfold.md (#21428), with four
decisions revised during implementation review and recorded in the doc:

- D4: nothing unfolds by default. The failure that explains the outcome is
  marked — rendered past the 50-row window and scrolled into view — but the
  reader opens it.
- D7: every line with a fold control toggles on click, the statement and the
  error included; only the unfolded block does not.
- D8: the section's box never changes height because a row unfolds. A block
  scrolls inside it, and its copy button is sticky to the box's top.
- D16: unfolding reveals what it opened by scrolling the section the least
  that shows the row; folding puts the line back where it was clicked from.

The model returns the line plus both payloads (verbatim statement and error)
instead of an 80-character cut; row keys are the entry's identity, assigned
once over the run so the reader's folds survive regrouping; the columns before
the statement are sized per section so the chevrons line up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(review): switch every standard rule on for a new workspace

CreateWorkspace inserts the workspace's REVIEW_RULE policy row, every
rule on and enforced, beside its IAM policy. The workspace SQL Review
page updates that row and gates on bb.policies.update alone; without
the row its first save went through CreatePolicy, which a role with
update but not create could not make.

Existing workspaces keep the GetPolicy stand-in and the store's
every-rule default; no migration.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(review): gate the workspace rules on update alone

Every workspace gets a review rule policy row by default, so a
workspace save is always an update. The page no longer lists policies
to learn whether the row exists, nor requires create as well when it
cannot list, and the store drops the list call added for that.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(review): keep inherited rules out of the set to restore

The read-only view shows rules set elsewhere. Following the workspace
in between switching customization off and on passed its rules through
the switches, which then restored them instead of the project's own
when SYNTAX went back on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(review): let a rule run complete while review is off

RunReview refused a rule run when the effective policy was empty, which
left the findings of earlier runs open forever once SYNTAX was switched
off: CompleteReviewRun resolves them only when a later run reaches DONE.
The run is now created as usual; the executor returns no findings for
an empty policy, so the run completes and clears the earlier ones.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(review): show the workspace rules link on the policy read alone

The V2 workspace SQL Review route needs only bb.policies.get, so the
link to it from the project page must not also require the v1
bb.reviewConfigs.list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(review): tell an absent policy from a failed refresh

- The policy store gains fetchPolicyByParentAndType, which resolves to
  null for a resource without a policy and to undefined when the read
  failed. The pages decide "failed" from that result, since a failed
  refresh leaves the earlier policy in the cache and the cache alone
  cannot tell the two apart.
- The rule switches are keyed by project or workspace, so the rules
  remembered while SYNTAX is off cannot carry over to another resource.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(review): read a policy the way the backend applies it

- A stored rule list without SYNTAX runs nothing, so it reads as empty
  on both pages instead of showing its rules as on.
- The project page reads the workspace policy only when this user holds
  bb.policies.get at workspace scope. Otherwise it loads from the
  project policy alone and says the inherited rules are not visible,
  instead of failing the whole page.
- Moving to another project, or workspace, drops an unsaved draft so it
  cannot be saved under the new name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(review): tell a missing policy row from a failed or unenforced read

The standard rule pages read a policy through GetPolicy, which stands
in for a missing workspace row, returns an unenforced row as-is, and
resolves to nothing when the transport fails. Each of those looked like
something else:

- A workspace policy switched off through the API rendered no switches,
  and a project following it showed no inherited rules. The backend
  applies every rule in that case, so the pages now do too.
- A failed read of either policy marked the project page loaded and
  showed "follows the workspace", where a save would have replaced the
  real policy. Both pages now show an error with a retry instead.
- An unenforced project row made the permission gate assume a create,
  while the save updates the row. The gate now follows row existence.
- The workspace gate required both create and update. It now lists the
  workspace's policies, including unenforced ones, to learn whether the
  row exists, and requires only the permission for that save; without
  the list permission it keeps requiring both.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(review): gate each rule save on the RPC it makes

Follow-ups from review:
- An unenforced REVIEW_RULE policy reads as absent, as the backend reads
  it, and a save re-enables it by putting enforce in the update mask.
- The workspace's first save creates its policy row, so editing needs
  bb.policies.create as well as bb.policies.update.
- On the project page, switching customization on is a create, editing
  the project's own rules an update, and switching it off a delete; each
  control follows its own permission, and undoing an unsaved switch
  needs none.
- The V2 SQL Review route requires bb.policies.get only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(review): switch the standard review rules on and off

SQL Review V2 keeps eleven standard rules behind one REVIEW_RULE policy,
and nothing in the product could switch them yet.

Backend:
- GetPolicy on a project without its own REVIEW_RULE policy is NOT_FOUND
  instead of the every-rule stand-in, so a client can tell "follows the
  workspace" from "customized to every rule". The workspace keeps the
  stand-in.
- SYNTAX gates the rest: GetEffectiveReviewRulePolicy returns an empty
  list when the nearest policy lacks it, RunReview refuses a RULE run
  with nothing on, and RuleExecutor returns no findings for an empty
  policy instead of asking omni, which evaluates SYNTAX regardless.

Frontend, in dev builds only behind sqlReviewV2Enabled():
- CI/CD > SQL Review shows the workspace rules as one centered card with
  a status line naming how many rules run, or that Syntax is off.
- A new project page under CI/CD > SQL Review follows the workspace by
  default and keeps the project's own list once "Customize for this
  project" is on; switching it back off deletes the project policy.
- Switching Syntax off saves an empty list; switching it on restores the
  session's previous set, else every rule.
- The v1 review policy surfaces (workspace create/detail routes, the
  project settings attach and "Enforce SQL review" toggle, the
  environment attach) are hidden.
- The policy store gains the REVIEW_RULE update mask it was missing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(frontend): keep the consent page's vertical padding on the spacing scale

The page took SplashLayout's py-12 (48px), which is outside the UX
contract's spacing vocabulary, whose largest step for a major page region
is 32px, and it spent 32px more of a short viewport above and below a
card that already scrolls there. Use py-8, the value the consent page
had before.

Found by Codex review.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(frontend): give the MCP consent card one width, centered on the viewport

The consent page sized itself as a fraction of SplashLayout's column
(md:w-3/5 lg:w-1/2), and that column is already half the viewport from
lg with 80-96px of padding, so on desktop screens the card came out
176-384px wide and every capability row wrapped (BYT-10284).

Consent is an interstitial, not a sign-in page: render it outside
SplashLayout, centered on the whole viewport, with a 672px card that
narrows only on screens that cannot hold it, and balance the header
text. SplashLayout now states the width contract for the pages that
stay in it.

Replace the unit test that pinned the fraction classes with an e2e spec
that measures the card at seven viewport widths.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(frontend): adapt to main's tooltip provider, semantic colors and MCP tables

Rebasing onto main brings #21522, which mounts one tooltip provider at the
app root, and the surfaces main reworked alongside it.

- `ProjectMaskingExemptionPage` and `IssueDetailCommentList` keep this
  branch's shared-clock reading and `HumanizeTs` rows, and take main's
  `text-warning` / `text-info` in place of raw palette colors.
- `CommentThreadCard`'s spec passes `issue`, the prop main renamed from
  `issueName`.
- main's MCP capability tables are keyed `read` and `write`, which the
  time-reading plugin reported: it rejected any object literal containing a
  `read`. A reading carries both members, so the literal check now keys on
  `nextChangeAt`, and shorthand `{ read }` -- a reading being unpacked or
  passed on -- keeps an alternative of its own. Probed each spelling:
  member access, optional chaining, a quoted key, both destructurings and a
  nested literal all still report; a table of flags no longer does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(frontend): measure a scroller's borders exactly, not from rounded widths

`fillableWidth` took the borders and scrollbar as `offsetWidth` less
`clientWidth`, which is exact only when they come to whole pixels. Chrome
snaps a 1px border to device pixels -- 0.8px at Windows 125%, 0.67px at
150% -- and the two rounded widths then differ by 1 or 2 for a true 1.6 or
1.33, so the access grants still scrolled on about a fifth of widths at
exactly the scales the previous commit was for.

Borders and padding now come from the computed style, which reports the
snapped values exactly. A scrollbar has no exact measure: what the two
rounded widths leave over the borders is a scrollbar only when it is more
than a pixel of rounding, and is then given one pixel more. Padding is
subtracted too, so the helper holds for a padded scroller as well.

Swept in a browser over 100 widths from 800 to 805px, with scale emulated
by CSS zoom on a DPR-2 display (1px border snapped to 0.8, 0.667 and
0.909px): the table scrolled 0 times at every scale, against 21-22 for the
previous measurement and 24-36 for `clientWidth`; with a 12px vertical
scrollbar and no border, 0 at every scale. The spec gains the snapped
border, a rounding remainder that looks like a scrollbar, and padding;
taking the borders from the rounded widths, ignoring padding, dropping the
scrollbar's pixel, reading any remainder as a scrollbar, or rounding
instead of flooring each fail it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(frontend): fit a table to the floor of its scroller's exact width

`clientWidth` rounds to a whole pixel, and a table half a pixel wider than
its scroller still scrolls. Every table fitted by `distributeColumnWidths`
-- the access grants and the schema editor's two -- was sized to it, and
since this branch makes the widths add up to exactly the measured width,
any fractional width that rounds up now scrolls: browser zoom, or Windows
at 125% or 150%, where a scrollbar that appears takes 12px of height.

`fillableWidth` is the one measurement all three use: the scroller's exact
width less its borders and any scrollbar, floored. Checked in a browser at
five fractional and whole widths, with and without a 12px vertical
scrollbar: `clientWidth` overran the exact inner width in eight of ten, and
`fillableWidth` fitted all ten, equal to `clientWidth` whenever the width is
whole. A spec pins the three cases; reading `clientWidth` again, rounding
instead of flooring, or ignoring the border each fail it.

The kept-space assertion in the HumanizeTs spec now checks only a piece with
a space at its edge, and accepts the class on an ancestor, so it fails when
the space would be dropped and not when an identical rendering moves the
class. The `truncate` comment names the one fallback it left out.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
